#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR enables the scheduler to reschedule unschedulable Pods when there are changes to node annotations.

issue_context.title: scheduler: add nodeAnnotationsChanged event to trigger rescheduling
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Due to limited character space, I've stored additional information in annotations on nodes. My custom scheduling plugins read these annotations to schedule Pods. However, when a Pod fails to be scheduled on a node, I want it to be removed from the Unschedulable queue. This can be achieved by modifying the annotations of the node, allowing the Pod to be rescheduled.

Unfortunately, the eventHandler of the scheduler only supports five types of node events, and it does not include the nodeAnnotationsChanged event. Consequently, I am currently unable to trigger rescheduling by changing the annotations of nodes.

/sig scheduling


### What did you expect to happen?

Unschedulable pods will be rescheduled after annotations of nodes changed.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

None

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

It's more like a new feature, not bug because it doesn't lead to any bad behavior on the upstream.

/remove-kind bug
/kind feature

My concern is node annotation is arbitrary, change a node annotation doesn't imply a pod is schedulable. But for other events, like node labels, node taints, they're the constraints we consider in scheduling. They're different, I'm afraid this will lead to invalid scheduling attempts.

Who is responsible for change the annotations in you scenario?

> They're different, I'm afraid this will lead to invalid scheduling attempts.

This enhancement has no impact on the in-tree plugins / upstream scheduler, right? 
Only (custom) plugins, that want to reschedule Pods via the node annotation change, will register `nodeAnnotationsChanged` event to EventsToRegister.

> Who is responsible for change the annotations in you scenario?

I have a controller capable of modifying node annotations to indicate node's current availability. And my custom plugins need to be aware of these changes.

> This enhancement has no impact on the in-tree plugins / upstream scheduler, right?

I guess we can still be impacted when scheduling pod failed because of no fit node rather than failed by the plugin. see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/34abd36e88e50d913af9413f9353515deb7f09d4/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L778-L780

> I have a controller capable of modifying node annotations to indicate node's current availability

Can we predict whether the pod is schedulable before running into scheduling cycle via the node annotations, then we can leverage the preEnqueue extension point since you already have a external controller. https://kubernetes.io/blog/2022/12/26/pod-scheduling-readiness-alpha/

> Can we predict whether the pod is schedulable before running into scheduling cycle via the node annotations, then we can leverage the preEnqueue extension point since you already have a external controller. https://kubernetes.io/blog/2022/12/26/pod-scheduling-readiness-alpha/

Thanks for the advice👍. But I'm afraid it would not be the best solution for us, because doing that outside the scheduling cycle would cause the custom plugins to malfunction in my scenario.

> This enhancement has no impact on the in-tree plugins / upstream scheduler, right?

The concerns raised by @kerthcet make sense to me.

In my understanding, most in-tree plugins will classify the event `nodeAnnotationsChanged` as an `Update` event.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a8d40a2f2521dd473028f432cacdb10819754e4e/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L61

> I guess we can still be impacted when scheduling pod failed because of no fit node rather than failed by the plugin. 

No. When no fit Pod, UnschedulablePlugins will have plugin(s) rejected the Pod. (e.g., all nodes don't have enough capacity, UnschedulablePlugins has noderesourcefit. all nodes don't satisfy node affinity, UnschedulablePlugins has nodeaffinity)
`len(pInfo.UnschedulablePlugins) != 0` is a rare case like plugins other than PreFilter/Filter returns non-success. 
I don't think we should care about it.

> most in-tree plugins will classify the event nodeAnnotationsChanged as an Update event.

But, this is a good point, I think we should refactor all plugins that register `Update` event with `Node` to have a specific Node update event.  For example, [node affinity](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeaffinity/node_affinity.go#L86). It should have `UpdateNodeLabel` with `Node` instead of `Update`.
`Update` event with `Node`, that should be the last-resort when we don't know which kind of Node update will make Pods schedulable. (I guess no such case at least in the in-tree plugins.)

> No. When no fit Pod, UnschedulablePlugins will have plugin(s) rejected the Pod

- 1) One possibility is Reserve Plugin, I added the capability here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118529
-  2) Another possibility is PreFilter, but not because failed by the plugin, but no fit node exists https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8aeea9c1b818825d3f01afe1c1c5907e6d76c515/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L665-L671

Have no idea whether we have other places, I guess no. But yes, this only impacts unschedulable pods has no failed plugins.

> For example, [node affinity](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeaffinity/node_affinity.go#L86). It should have UpdateNodeLabel with Node instead of Update.

~I think this is for intended, like ~
~1. 1) we have a plugin failed by nodeAffinity~
~2. 2) we add a new node~
~3. 3) we receive the node add event, but because node not ready, we failed by nodeTaint plugin as `nodeNotReady`~
4. 4) node become ready, we get the node update event, but dismatch with nodeAffinity registered event (if we registered with UpdateNodeLabel event)~
~5. 5) pod will not be moved to the active or backoff queue~

updated below https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/118369#issuecomment-1581140381

weigh in @alculquicondor for advices as whether this is a good idea to take nodeAnnotations as a new event. As I know, some plugins will read the embedded prometheus metrics in node annotations for scoring, but not for filtering.

At least we should mitigate the impacts.

> iii. we receive the node add event, but because node not ready, we failed by nodeTaint plugin as nodeNotReady
iv. node become ready, we get the node update event, but dismatch with nodeAffinity registered event (if we registered with UpdateNodeLabel event)

(3) is not exact. When we receive the node add event, the scheduler retry to schedule the Pod because the nodeaffinity has Node add event. And it's rejected by the nodetaint plugin. (not node affinity)
So, in (4), we get the node update event, it matches with node taint registered event, and the Pod is moved to active/backoffQ (node taint registers node update event. Yes I think we can change node taint's node update event to more specific one(s) though)

> One possibility is Reserve Plugin

As I replied in your PR, we acknowledged that in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117844, and yes let's have your patch.

> Another possibility is PreFilter, but not because failed by the plugin, but no fit node exists

Well, that's a good point. So, when all nodes are filtered out by PreFilterResult, then no failedplugin can be returned. That's a problem. I think we should return the plugin name that returns PreFilterResult with not all Node names in this case (= the plugins that contributes to reducing the candidate Nodes via PreFilterResult). What do you think?

Sorry, the previous one is not right, a detailed one:

a. we have a pod failed by nodeAffinity. pod will be placed into the unschedulablePods
b. node autoscaler triggered, a new node added, emitted a node add event
c. called `MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue` -> `preCheckForNode`
d. node not ready right now and holds a notReady taint, then `preCheckForNode` failed, pod still stays in the unschedulablePods
e. node gets ready, emitted a node update event, but dismatch with the registered event(if we register with `UpdateNodeLabel` in nodeAffinity plugin)
f. pod will stay in unschedulabelPods

I guess this is the right flow. Anyway, glad to see it be more effect in the future.
If we have no performance problems, I think it's ok to take nodeAnnotations into consideration.

Wouldn't this be solved with @sanposhiho's proposal on ClusterEventWithHint? #117844

If so, I prefer we leave the existing code as-is.
whatever we do here, we wouldn't backport, so I think #117844 is the right move forward.

We put many stuff here. Let me summarize each:

### 1. change node `Update` to a specific `UpdateXXXX` event

Born from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/118369#issuecomment-1579851665

[The last comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/118369#issuecomment-1581140381) from @kerthcet is right. But, that's the problem with preCheck. (Some preCheck depends on some in-tree plugins' logic and it affects badly to other plugins enqueueing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110175)
The preCheck is removed after https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117844 is completed. After preCheck is removed, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/118369#issuecomment-1581103551 will be the correct behavior. So, we can do the optimization that changes node `Update` to a specific `UpdateXXXX` event. 

### 2. plugin failed in `Reserve` isn't registered in unschedulable plugins.

will be fixed in: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118529

### 3. If PreFilter's PreFilterResult filter out all Nodes, no unschedulable plugin is registered

It's kind of rare case, but I feel we need to have some improvement like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/118369#issuecomment-1581129204

Edit: create another issue for this: 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122018

---

I'd say (2) and (3) are kind of rare cases. So, the blocker here is (1). (And, (1) is blocked by the removal of preCheck, which is blocked by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117844.)
As my conclusion, it's safer to add `nodeAnnotationsChanged` after (1) is done so that we can make sure the performance won't be affected badly.
@kerthcet what do you think?
Instead, can we just keep an event for "node updated", then individual plugins can decide whether a annotations change is worth requeuing or not?

Yes, (1) can be replaced with that idea. But, I'd say changing to a specific `UpdateXXXX` is slightly better because the scheduling queue could filter out some Node update events without executing the hint functions.
If rescheduling can be triggered with precise events, that would be great. I haven't revisit https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117844 since last time, I'll take a look again.

Since we are missing an event for `NodeUpdate`, can we add it?

```golang
# in pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/events.go
NodeUpdate = framework.ClusterEvent{Resource: framework.Node, ActionType: framework.Add, Label: "NodeAdd"}
```

But we also have to modify existing events like so:
```golang
NodeSpecUnschedulableChange = framework.ClusterEvent{Resource: framework.Node, ActionType: framework.UpdateNodeTaint|framework.Update, Label: "NodeSpecUnschedulableChange"}
```

Because change of such field is also an Update.

And in future releases we can get rid of some fine-grained events.

Since we will **add hintFuncs for all in-tree plugins**, so I think it's ok to add nodeAnnotationsChanged event now, we can filter out unrelated events in hitFuncs. Any other concerns? cc @alculquicondor  @sanposhiho 

> And in future releases we can get rid of some fine-grained events

Prefer to keep them as people can register fine-gained events instead a general `nodeUpdate` event.
If by "now" you mean v1.30, then I'm ok with that.

If that's the case, we should also pass events to [SchedulingQueue.MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L764) since it currently processes only one event at a time.
